# Regional Hospital Stroke Capabilities (WWAMI)

Static, public-source reference atlas of hospital stroke capability in
Washington, Alaska, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming: national stroke certification,
state stroke designation, documented thrombectomy (EVT) and 24/7 EVT, kept as
separate claims with sources and check dates, plus straight-line access to
receiving centers and transparent, adjustable planning scenarios.

<!-- counts:start -->262 facility records (WA 97, AK 24, ID 47, MT 63, WY 31): 142 in the adult emergency-stroke analysis set, 9 excluded with a documented reason, 111 with eligibility unresolved; 1 not yet located. Stroke capability: 235 assessed, 10 partly assessed, 7 not assessed, 10 with conflicting evidence; 19 with documented 24/7 thrombectomy. 8 receiving centers outside the five states are included as destinations only. Data 2026.10.17.1, evidence review 2026-10-17.<!-- counts:end -->

- Site: https://rkalani1.github.io/telestroke-expansion-map/
- Source: https://github.com/rkalani1/telestroke-expansion-map

## Data

- /hospitals.json — the dataset the app loads (schema 4.0.0). Read its
  top-level definitions before interpreting records: date_semantics,
  claim_states, methods, eligibility_rule, tier_crosswalk, road_networks,
  census_snapshot, scope, counts, sources.
- One record per hospital CAMPUS (stable `id`; `previousIds` lists retired
  ids). CCN, NPI, address and coordinates are separate fields; `ccn.relation`
  says whether the campus bills under its own or a parent's CCN.
- Every material fact is a CLAIM with a state — affirmative, negative (verified
  absent within a stated scope), no-record-found (searched, nothing found; NOT
  proof of absence), unknown (not assessed, or searched and still unresolved;
  NEVER read as "no"), conflicting, not-applicable — plus evidence (source
  ids into `sources`, excerpts), a `checked` date and a `method`. Claims:
  status, address, location, serviceType, population, cah, ed, governance,
  system, national, stateDesignation, evt, evt247, roadNetwork.
- National certification and state designation are different things. The
  display tier (`derived.tier`) comes from the national certification when
  documented, otherwise from a WA ECS or Idaho TSE level through a published
  DISPLAY crosswalk (`derived.tierBasis = state-crosswalk`), which does not
  mean the hospital holds that national certification.
- `derived.eligibility` defines the adult emergency-stroke analysis set:
  eligible (active + a 24/7 general ED + serving adults; the ED is documented
  for the campus or inferred from a program requirement: the Critical Access
  Hospital or Rural Emergency Hospital conditions of participation, or the
  Washington stroke Level II criteria), excluded (with a reason), or
  unresolved. A VA or military hospital with such an ED is unresolved with
  code `restricted-access` (civilian and EMS access not documented) and can
  still be a receiving destination. Count unresolved records as unresolved,
  not as eligible or excluded.
- Dates: `checked` is when a claim was compared with its evidence (null =
  never, or not recorded); `evidence_review_date` is the latest review pass,
  not a date every record was verified; `generated` is when curated inputs
  last changed. Many claims are carried forward from the previous edition
  (`method: prior-edition`): they keep that edition's date as `editionAsOf`
  and have `checked` null, an edition date, not a claim-level check date.
- /data/audit/evidence-audit.csv — one row per facility x claim with the
  outcome of the October 2026 review: confirmed, corroborated, established,
  corrected, carried-forward, conflicting, searched-unresolved (searched in
  this review and still unknown, including an earlier value that could not be
  confirmed), inaccessible, not-assessed or missing.
- /data/verification-worklist.csv — ranked open checks, each naming the
  source that can settle it.

## Methods

- /METHODOLOGY.md — records and the census denominator, separate dimensions,
  evidence and dates, the analysis set, geography, straight-line distances and
  destination sets, illustrative transport scenarios, the access review,
  checks and limits.
- /docs/SCHEMA.md — every field. /docs/SOURCE-MAINTENANCE.md — how claims are
  re-checked. /CHANGELOG.md — releases. /COMPLIANCE.md — public-data boundary.

## Scope

Public-source planning reference. Not for clinical decision-making, patient
routing or dispatch, and not an official health-department or accreditor
product. It records no institutional approval, affiliation, referral
agreement, contract or real-time availability. Distances are straight-line;
lines are geometry, not routes or referral relationships; transport times are
illustrative scenarios, never compared with treatment-time targets. The
access review ranks questions to investigate, not hospitals to approach.
